title: A Personalised Anti-fatigue Program for Community-dwelling People With Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia
official: Assessment of a Personalised Anti-fatigue Multimodal Program for Community-dwelling People With Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia: a Pilot Feasibility Study
summary:
The goal of this pilot study is to learn if a personalised, home-based online physical activity program (LIVE-CLL) is feasible for adults with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL) who experience fatigue. It will also learn if the program improves fatigue, symptoms and quality of life. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can people with CLL be recruited to the program, attend their prescribed sessions, follow the prescribed exercise intensities, and stay in the study? Do fatigue, symptoms and quality of life change after 12 weeks of the program?

All participants will receive the LIVE-CLL program alongside their usual care. Researchers will compare measurements taken before and after the program.

Participants will:

Complete online fitness assessments and questionnaires by video call before and after the program Follow a personalised 12-week aerobic and strength program at home, 3 to 5 sessions per week, delivered through an exercise app Complete a short check-in form before each session and a wellbeing form each week, so the program can be adjusted

interventions.name: LIVE-CLL personalised home-based physical activity program

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Aged 18 years or older
* Confirmed diagnosis of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL), including small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), according to International Workshop on CLL (iwCLL) guidelines
* Clinically relevant fatigue, defined as a FACIT-Fatigue total score of less than 34
* Either treatment-naïve or currently receiving CLL treatment, and not expected to change treatment pathway during the 12-week study (e.g., starting treatment or completing fixed-duration therapy)
* Able to provide written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

No access to the digital platforms used to assess participants and deliver the program (e.g., internet-connected device for video calls and the exercise app)

* Absolute contraindications to physical activity, including self-reported:
* Acute cardiac event within the past 6 months
* Unstable angina
* Uncontrolled dysrhythmias causing symptoms or haemodynamic compromise
* Symptomatic aortic stenosis
* Uncontrolled symptomatic heart failure
* Acute pulmonary embolus
* Acute myocarditis or pericarditis
* Suspected or known dissecting aneurysm
* Acute systemic infection
* Participants flagged by the PAR-Q+ / ePARmed-X+ as requiring medical clearance, who do not receive clearance to exercise from their healthcare provider
